formalDefinition: For a weighted graph G = (V,E), with non-negative edge weights, a source vertex s ∈ V, find the shortest path distance from s to every other vertex v ∈ V, where path length is defined as the sum of edge weights along the path.
problemDefinition: Single Source Shortest Path (SSSP) in a weighted graph is the problem of determining the shortest path from a source vertex to all other reachable vertices in the graph such that the sum of edge weights along each path is minimized.
inputDescription: A weighted graph and a source vertex
outputDescription: The shortest path from the source vertex to every other reachable vertex in the graph
instanceFormat: Format: (N,E,s) | N is set, E subset N unorderedcross N or N cross N (edges optionally weighted as (edge,weight), non-negative only), s in N Example: ({1,2,3,4,5},{((1,2),4),((1,3),2),((2,3),1),((3,5),7),((2,4),3),((4,5),9)},1) Parallel edges: when two edges join the same nodes (in the same direction, if directed), the lightest one is used.
certificateFormat: Format: {(node,path)} | one pair per node in N, path is {q0,...,qn} shortest from s to node, or {} if unreachable Example: {(1,{1}),(2,{1,2}),(3,{1,3}),(4,{1,2,4}),(5,{1,3,5})}
